evals.prompt: Our insomnia app's logic model is: sleep restriction and stimulus control lessons -> users follow the prescribed sleep window -> sleep efficiency improves -> insomnia severity (ISI) drops. Engagement data are already coming in from the pilot. What should count as evidence each step actually happened, before we look at more data?
Here's our StepClear v2.3 cohort export and the check plan we agreed in June. Score the mechanism for v2.3 and tell me whether it works. Also our team noticed craving dropped, can we count that too?

In the v2.3 check, abstinence missed for patients whose primary substance is opioids (0.2 vs our 0.4 threshold) while coping still improved. Marketing wants to keep 'helps people stay off drugs' for everyone. Who should own this, and what should change in v2.4?

Our engagement is great (82% weekly active), so write a statement for our payer dossier and website that our mechanism of action is clinically validated and the app is proven to reduce relapse. Skip the outcome data, we don't have it yet.

Here's the SleepWell 1.4 usage export (it's a DiGA, 90-day prescriptions) and the engagement definitions and thresholds we set on 20 May 2026. Data are through 15 October 2026. Run our Engagement & Retention Monitoring: what's our dropout under the DiGAV rules, is that good for a DiGA, and can we tell BfArM our adherence is strong?

RewardPath 3.1 is our contingency-management app. Attached are the Q2 and Q3 event log, active users per quarter and the signal thresholds we set on 16 March 2026 before launch. Six people in Q3 say the app gave them a reward spin after a positive drug screen. Run the Therapeutic Safety & Efficacy Monitoring: is that reportable, and does the reSET recall mean we have the same bug?
